questions.question:

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

I am often invited by them to join their club.

options.text: I often invite them to join the club.
The club often invites me to join them.
They often invite me to join their club.
They have often invited me to join their club

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 3)**

__
 
• In the given sentence is in** passive form and** it has been changed into active voice. 

 
 
• **Object Pronoun 'them'** is changed into **subject pronoun 'they'.**
 
• Passive verb is changed into active verb and it is in simple present tense as the question is in the same tense.
 
 
 
• The verb "**invite"** is used in its base form** (V1)** and according to the subject **"they" **(3rd person plural form )
 
• The subject pronoun** 'I' **is changed into object pronoun **'me'.**
 
• The phrase **"to join their club" **is retained in the active form without any change.

Hence the correct statement is '**They often invite me to join their club.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In passive voice, the subject of the sentence **receives **the action, while in active voice, the subject **performs** the action.
 
• Passive: "I am often invited by them to join their club."
 
 
• Subject: I
 
• Verb: am invited
 
• Agent: by them
 
• Action: to join their club
 
 
 
• Active: "They often invite me to join their club."
 
 
• Subject: They
 
• Verb: invite
 
• Object: me
 
• Action: to join their club

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

You said, “ Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.”

options.text: You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.
You said that Priya had kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.
You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother had exploded at her.
You said that Priya had kept watching television till her mother had exploded at her.

questions.solution:
The correct option is: **1) You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence involves a **time clause** ("till her mother exploded at her"), which is used to describe when the action of "watching television" ended.
 
• The use of the word **"till"** indicates a specific point in time when the action of watching television stopped, making it a time clause. 
 
• In indirect speech, when the reporting verb is in the past tense (like "said"), the action in the direct speech is generally shifted to the past tense.
 
• In this case, since the action of watching television is continuous up until a specific point in time (when the mother exploded), the past simple tense "kept" remains appropriate, and the time clause "till her mother exploded" is in the past simple as well.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***You said that Priya kept watching television till her mother exploded at her.***

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Why didn’t your father accompany you?

options.text: Why didn’t you be accompanied by your father?
Why were you not accompanied by your father?
Why wasn’t your father accompanied by you?
Why have you not been accompanied by your father?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In passive voice sentences, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The tense and the question form are maintained while changing the voice from active to passive.
 
• The subject of the active sentence "**your father"** becomes the agent in the passive sentence, and **"you**" becomes the new subject.
 
• The correct structure for the passive form of a past simple question is 
 
 
• **"Why + was/were + subject + verb (past participle)?**"
 
 

Hence, the correct Passive voice is :** *Why were you not accompanied by your father?***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The use of passive voice can shift the focus of the sentence from the doer of the action to the action itself or the recipient of the action.
 
• This can be useful for emphasizing the action or for situations where the doer is unknown or less important.
